title: streamctx: composable cancellation helpers and backoff-aware stream readers for SDK ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a small, well-documented helper package (streamctx) in the Go SDK that provides composable cancellation primitives and a backoff-aware stream reader wrapper. Goal is to make common streaming patterns (graceful shutdown, per-message deadlines, cooperative backoff, and idempotent retry boundaries) easy for application teams while keeping runtime behavior predictable and testable.

Motivation: Many internal tickets and customer reports show confusion about how to wire context cancellations from controllers into long-lived streaming handlers without leaking goroutines or causing head-of-line timeouts. We also see brittle retry behavior when network flaps cause transient EOFs during long streams; teams either over-retry (duplicating messages) or under-retry (losing availability). A small helper with examples should drastically reduce user errors and support better SDK default behaviors.

Scope:
- Package: internal/streamctx (exported via sdk/streamctx) with stable, well-documented surface.
- Features: composable cancel scopes, WithPerMessageDeadline convenience, BackoffAwareReader wrapper that coordinates exponential backoff with parent request-level deadlines, Idempotency boundary helper for consumer-side replay-safe reads.
- Examples: two runnable examples in /examples/streaming: graceful_shutdown_server.go and resilient_consumer.go.
- Tests: unit tests for context propagation, simulated network flaps with deterministic clock, and integration test against local streaming test harness.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Composable scopes vs single global context: We provide a light-weight CancelScope type that holds a context and a CancelFunc and implements a Join(other) operation so higher-level controllers can attach short-lived per-message deadlines without losing the root request context. We considered a purely functional approach (returning derived contexts everywhere) but found ergonomics poorer for users wiring middleware.
- Per-message deadlines: Default API is to attach a short per-message deadline (e.g., 3s) for downstream processing while honoring the overall request deadline. This prevents one slow message from blocking the lifetime of the stream. Downsides: more cancellations visible to users; mitigated by clear docs and examples.
- BackoffAwareReader semantics: Wrapper returns io.EOF only when the server signalled end-of-stream; on transient connection errors it will surface a typed transient error (streamctx.ErrTransient) which callers can use with streamctx.IdempotentBoundary to safely retry from last acked sequence. We debated automatic in-wrapper retries, but that would hide network behavior and potentially duplicate messages for non-idempotent consumers. Instead we expose helpers and an example retry loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- streamctx package implemented and exported in go-sdk v0.8.
- 90%+ unit coverage for helpers and deterministic tests for Join/WithPerMessageDeadline semantics.
- Two end-user examples demonstrating graceful shutdown and backoff-aware retry loop; placed in examples/streaming with README.
- PR + design doc reviewed and merged, follow-on issue to port to TypeScript SDK patterns.

Links:
- Design doc (internal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/streamctx+design (placeholder)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/pull/789
- Streaming test harness dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/streaming-test/harness (internal)

Low-level API sketch (for reviewers):
```go
// CancelScope represents a composable cancellation boundary
type CancelScope struct {
    Ctx context.Context
    Cancel func()
}

// NewScope(ctx) returns a CancelScope tied to ctx
// s.Join(other) makes s cancel when either s or other cancels
// WithPerMessageDeadline(s, dur) returns a derived scope for single message work

// BackoffAwareReader wraps an io.ReadCloser from the transport
// On transient connection errors returns ErrTransient instead of io.EOF
// Caller drives a retry loop keyed by an idempotency token and lastAckedSeq
```
Implementation notes: use go-stepbackoff deterministic clock in tests; keep runtime path allocation-free for fastpath (no heap allocation per message in steady state). Avoid hidden goroutine timers by using a single timer per scope where possible.
comments: 2025-11-06 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial design after pairing with Liam. Chosen CancelScope API to balance ergonomics and explicitness.

2025-12-01 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented prototype and basic tests. Observed that WithPerMessageDeadline caused spike in timer allocations under synthetic load. Optimized by reusing timers via pool (WIP).

2026-01-18 - Marina Chen (reviewer): Asked for clearer error typing for transient vs terminal stream errors; requested ErrTransient, ErrTerminal typed errors and examples showing how to map to user retry policies.
2026-02-04 - Security review: no cryptographic changes; surface reviewed. Marked low risk.

2026-03-02 - QA (Ben Torres): Integration test against harness shows recovered streams after simulated 250ms flaps with backoff loop; one flaky test around Join() race observed and fixed (moved cancel propagation to atomic flag).
notes: Follow-up: after merge, schedule a 1-hour office-hours demo with SDK consumers and create a TypeScript SDK parity ticket. Also add a short blurb to the Release Notes highlighting the new guards against duplicate processing during transient network failures.
